summary: conv-context-next preinstall fetches Bun runtime to execute obfuscated bundled payload
details: package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime binary from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases (v1.3.13), extracts it to a temporary directory, chmods it executable, and immediately execs it against the shipped math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB single-line `// @bun @bun-cjs` file using rotated string-array obfuscation (dispatcher `WV8StW` push/shift-rotates the `n7gIxM` constant array) and hex-named identifiers. The `@bun-cjs` header indicates the payload is not intended to run under Node — a second language runtime is fetched at preinstall time solely to execute this opaque blob. The package advertises itself as a small conversation-context/lodash-adjacent library, which does not require Bun for any legitimate build step. The combination of preinstall trigger, alternate-runtime download, heavy obfuscation, and purpose mismatch is an install-time dropper: on `npm install`, arbitrary attacker-authored code executes on the installer's machine under a runtime that bypasses Node-based install-time analyzers.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
